finding.claim: Exponential-time fragment traversal in the validation-rule extensions (QueryDepthLimiter, and MaxAliasesLimiter with the same pattern). Fragment expansion is not memoized, and `visited_fragments` only guards the current path, so cycles are caught but a DAG is walked once per path. A document with a chain of fragments, each spreading the next one twice (`fragment f0 on Query { ...f1 ...f1 } fragment f1 on Query { ...f2 ...f2 } ... fragment fN on Query { __typename }`), costs O(2^N) steps. Spreads do not increase `depth_so_far`, so the `depth_so_far > max_depth` cutoff never fires. The limiter meant to protect the server therefore becomes a CPU-exhaustion vector: an unauthenticated request of a few hundred bytes pins a worker.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled GraphQL query text in the HTTP POST/GET body or a websocket subscribe message (unauthenticated where the endpoint is public). The server must have QueryDepthLimiter or MaxAliasesLimiter enabled.
finding.sink: determine_depth() in query_depth_limiter.py recursing through FragmentSpreadNode with no cache. count_fields_with_alias() in max_aliases.py recurses the same way.

trace.note: schema.execute is called with the attacker's query text
_run_validation runs after parsing, once the operation type has been checked
DepthLimitValidator.__init__ computes depths for all operations in the document
determine_depth is called for each operation
FragmentSpreadNode branch recurses into the fragment with depth_so_far unchanged and visited_fragments extended only for the current path, so every path through the fragment DAG is re-walked
Fragment and inline-fragment definitions iterate all selections, doubling the work per level
Same unmemoized fragment recursion; there is no depth bound at all

finding.guards_checked: The depth_so_far > max_depth check (query_depth_limiter.py:231) only counts field nesting, not fragment-only chains. visited_fragments (:274, :285) is per-path, so it stops cycles but not DAG fan-out. max_tokens, if configured, bounds query size but the doubling chain fits in a few hundred tokens. The schema validation rules (NoFragmentCycles etc.) do not stop a valid fragment DAG. Rule constructors run before the visitor starts, so the cost is paid even if another rule would reject the document. I did not execute a PoC; this is based on reading the code.
